sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Spokane Valley?
sections.html:
Spokane Valley is the largest suburb of Spokane and was the ninth-most populous city in Washington at the 2020 census. The Census Bureau estimates 108,405 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 5.2 percent from the 2020 base. The city covers 37.72 square miles of land along the Spokane River, east of Spokane and west of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, and it surrounds the separate city of Millwood on three sides. Locals call it "The Valley."

This table sets the city beside Seattle using Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024, so you can see how different the two markets are.

sections.h2: How did Spokane Valley become a city?
sections.html:
It became a city in 2003 by combining several unincorporated communities, and that history explains the mix of housing you see today. The Valley was farm and orchard country first, irrigated beginning in 1895. In 1940 about 10,000 people lived there, by 1960 roughly 45,000, and by 1970 the suburb held 60,000.

Voters approved incorporation on May 21, 2002, after four failed attempts. The City of Spokane Valley was incorporated on March 31, 2003, combining Dishman, Opportunity, Trentwood, Veradale, part of Greenacres and East Spokane, with Yardley and Chester also inside the boundaries. At that point it was the third-largest newly incorporated city in United States history. Supporters wanted a stronger local voice and feared annexation by Spokane, while opponents pointed to the risk of higher taxes.

Because the city grew in stages, its streets include many curved and discontinuous roads and cul-de-sacs, typical of postwar suburbs. The city sits at 2,038 feet. Precipitation averages just over 16 inches a year, July is the warmest month at an average of 73 degrees, and January averages 28.3 degrees.

sections.h2: Which roads and transit routes serve Spokane Valley?
sections.html:
Interstate 90 is the backbone, and the city is reached from exits 285 through 293. Commutes are short by regional standards, averaging 20.8 minutes. These are the corridors buyers mention most:

  • Sprague Avenue, the main retail corridor, also carries the Interstate 90 Business designation.
  • Trent Avenue is State Route 290 and runs northeast to the Idaho border.
  • Pines Road is the northern end of State Route 27, part of the Palouse Scenic Byway.
  • North to south arterials include Argonne and Mullan roads, Pines, Evergreen and Sullivan.
  • Spokane Transit Authority serves the city through the Pence-Cole Valley Transit Center, with a few park-and-ride locations.

Spokane International Airport is about 16 miles west in Spokane, and Felts Field, a general aviation airport, is on the city's northern edge. The state transportation department began installing ramp meters on Interstate 90 in 2019 to ease peak congestion, and the state reports increasing congestion at peak commute hours.

sections.h2: Which school districts cover Spokane Valley?
sections.html:
Several districts share the city. The Central Valley School District is the largest, with 14,593 students in preschool through twelfth grade, followed by the East Valley School District with 4,277 and the West Valley School District with 3,862. A portion of western Spokane Valley falls within Spokane Public Schools. Boundaries do not follow city limits, so confirm the district for your address before you describe the schools in a listing.

Private options include Valley Christian School and The Oaks Academy. Juniors and seniors can attend Spokane Valley Tech, a skills center supported by area districts, and Carrington College has a campus in the city. Residents also have a Spokane County Library District branch inside city limits. Adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher at a rate of 26.5 percent.

sections.h2: What does the city require for permits and business licenses?
sections.html:
The city requires a permit for new homes, duplexes, garages, decks, pools, spas and fences, and for any addition or interior alteration to a home. That last point matters if you changed the interior yourself. The Permit Center is at City Hall, 10210 E. Sprague Avenue, and the phone number is 509-720-5240. Applicants submit site plans and construction plans, along with a copy of the sewer permit, which Spokane County Utilities issues. Applications can be filed through the online portal, and paid by credit card (with a 2.5 percent convenience fee) or by check.

Spokane Valley requires every business to hold a state business license that is renewed each year, and the city's general license fee is $25 to start and $25 to renew. A home business needs its own permit. If you rent out the house, ask the city's Business Licensing Specialist at 509-720-5333 whether a rental needs a license or registration.

If you plan to sell a single-family rental with a tenant in it, RCW 59.18.650 requires at least 90 days' written notice, and the owner must list the house within 30 days after the tenant leaves.

sections.h2: What taxes and recording steps apply when I sell?
sections.html:
You pay through the Spokane County Treasurer, and the sequence matters. Washington's real estate excise tax applies to nearly every sale, and the county requires a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit and the deed to go to the Treasurer's office before the deed is presented to the Spokane County Auditor for recording. The county takes cash or a check payable to the Spokane County Treasurer and asks you not to mail cash. The Treasurer's number is 509-477-4713.

The state portion is 1.1 percent on the part of the price up to $525,000, and higher rates apply above that. At the $382,300 Census median value, the state tax would be about $4,205, which is below the first break point. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, that break point rises to $551,000. A local rate is added on top, so ask the Treasurer or your closing agent for the figure. The seller usually pays, and the state treats the date the deed is notarized as the date of sale. Interest runs if payment is not made within one month.

Property tax runs on a separate schedule. Spokane County bills once a year with two payment coupons:

  • The first half is due April 30 and the second half is due October 31.
  • If the tax is under $50, the full amount is due April 30.
  • When a due date falls on a weekend or county holiday, the county accepts payment the next business day.
  • Both 2026 dates have passed, so the next one is April 30, 2027.
  • If no statement arrives by March 31, look it up on the county's SCOUT system or call the Treasurer.

You will also give the buyer the state seller disclosure statement within five business days after contract acceptance, and the buyer has three business days to rescind unless that right is waived. If the house needs repairs you would rather not make, you can request a cash offer for your Spokane Valley house and compare it with a listed sale.

faqs.q: How many people live in Spokane Valley, WA?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 108,405 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 102,976, and the city incorporated on March 31, 2003.

faqs.q: When are Spokane County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due April 30 and the second half is due October 31. If the bill is under $50, the whole amount is due April 30. A due date that lands on a weekend or county holiday moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: How do I pay the real estate excise tax on a Spokane Valley sale?
faqs.a: Take the excise tax affidavit and the deed to the Spokane County Treasurer's office before the deed goes to the Auditor for recording. Payment is by cash or a check payable to the Spokane County Treasurer. Do not mail cash.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remodel before selling in Spokane Valley?
faqs.a: Yes, the city lists any interior alteration to a home, duplex or accessory structure as work that needs a residential permit. Additions, decks, pools, spas and fences also need one. Contact the Permit Center at 509-720-5240.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Spokane Valley house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Central Valley, East Valley and West Valley serve most of the city, and part of the western edge is in Spokane Public Schools. Check the district's boundary map before you put a school name in a listing.
